question: Should OpenClaw accept the proposed Claw package, manifest, ownership, and lifecycle contract as the product direction and transition RFC 0016 from draft to accepted?
rationale: The patch is internally coherent, but accepting it commits multiple repositories and future package authors to a new user-facing CLI and durable compatibility model; repository policy reserves that transition for explicit maintainer acceptance.

options.title: Accept and transition
options.body: Approve the complete-agent package model, create the implementation tracking issue, update the RFC metadata to `accepted`, and merge the RFC with both v1 specifications.

options.title: Continue incubation
options.body: Keep the RFC open as `draft` and the implementations experimentally gated while maintainers narrow or revise the contract.

options.title: Narrow the initial contract
options.body: Accept a smaller add and export manifest subset now while deferring update, removal, registry, or cross-owner lifecycle guarantees.

recommendation.title: Accept and transition
recommendation.body: Approve the complete-agent package model, create the implementation tracking issue, update the RFC metadata to `accepted`, and merge the RFC with both v1 specifications.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main ownership signal is the adjacent plugin and MCP lifecycle surface that the RFC deliberately composes with, while final acceptance still requires an authorized repository maintainer.
